name: Amur Stonechat
rangeDescription: Eastern siberia to japan and korea; winters to southern china and indochina
description: A chunky little bird found in a wide variety of open landscapes, often sitting on exposed perches. Breeding male has a black head, a broad white half-collar, mostly rusty-red underparts, and a white undertail and rump.

name: Tawny-browed Owl
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Large brown owl with dark eyes and distinctive white semicircles on its face. Streaked below with distinctive pale white bars.

name: White-fronted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Arid southeastern peru (puno?) to northern argentina, paraguay, and southwestern brazil
description: Medium-sized pied woodpecker. Has a white forehead and a yellow or white throat and is grayish below with a barred mantle and tail.

name: Short-tailed Grasswren
rangeDescription: Stony hillsides of flinders and gawler ranges (south australia)
description: Small, pale, streaked bird with darker face and long cocked tail (albeit a bit shorter than in other grasswrens), found in hilly areas and ridgelines with spinifex clumps in the Flinders and Gawler ranges in South Australia. Similar to Striated Grasswren but with a shorter tail and slightly thicker bill.

name: Coquerel's Coua
rangeDescription: Humid and dry deciduous forest of western madagascar
description: Long-tailed, long-legged understory bird. Rufous belly and all-blue bare facial skin.

name: Pacific Antwren
rangeDescription: Panama (veraguas) to coastal pacific colombia and western ecuador
description: A small, short-tailed antwren found from western Panama to Ecuador. Male is entirely streaked black and white, with two white wingbars.

name: Streak-breasted Treehunter
rangeDescription: Central highlands of costa rica and western panama
description: This warm brown forest dweller is similar to many other foliage-gleaners and treehunters. Look for the relatively bright orangey throat with streaking on the breast.

name: Cameroon Pigeon
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern nigeria and southwestern cameroon
description: A large dark purple-gray pigeon with distinctive white spots on the breast and back, a blue-gray head, and a bright red-and-yellow bill. Often seen flying over the canopy in transit or during display flights, and sometimes perches conspicuously in the open.
imageCreditName: Stu Elsom - Stuart Elsom Ecology / Rockjumper Birding Tours

name: White-throated Manakin
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny, inconspicuous manakin of lowland rainforest canopy. Adult male is unmistakable; females and young males are told by slim shape and crisp two-toned appearance.

name: Grauer's Warbler
rangeDescription: Dense montane forest of eastern democratic republic of the congo, southwestern uganda, and western rwanda
description: Taxonomically unusual though not very boldly marked warbler. In poor light, or at a distance, looks dingy overall.

name: Cinnamon-chested Bee-eater
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern africa
description: Colorful, medium-sized bee-eater with rich rufous underparts. In flight, shows black patches at the back of the wings and sides of the tail.

name: Gray-bellied Hawk
rangeDescription: Locally in humid forest of south america east of the andes
description: Rare, unobtrusive, and robust forest hawk. Dark above and pale below with gleaming white underwings.

name: Black-chinned Yuhina
rangeDescription: Northern india eastward to central and southeastern china, southward to western myanmar, northern and central laos, vietnam, and far eastern cambodia
description: A small yuhina of open forest environments. Black chin is not very noticeable, but the black crest is.

name: White-naped Seedeater
rangeDescription: Savanna of eastern colombia to southern venezuela and northwestern amazonian brazil
description: Large seedeater with a thick white bill. Males are black above and white below.

name: White-browed Hawk
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern peru, northern bolivia, and southern amazonian brazil
description: Compact, black-and-white forest hawk. Short tail and broad wings give it a chunkier appearance than other interior forest raptors like forest-falcons and hawks in the genus Accipiter.

name: White-fronted Chat
rangeDescription: Southern australia including tasmania, and king and flinders islands
description: A small bird patterned in black, white, and gray. Adult males have white underparts and face contrasting with an obvious black neck-band which extends around from the back of the head.

name: Plumbeous Warbler
rangeDescription: Guadeloupe including terre-de-haut and marie-galante (just to south of guadeloupe) and dominica (central lesser antilles)
description: A striking small bird that frequents montane forests, but sometimes ventures into dry scrub and mangroves. This species is readily distinguished by its overall gray plumage (tinged green above and yellow below on immature birds) with boldly contrasting white eyebrows and wingbars.

name: Vinaceous Rosefinch
rangeDescription: Western china (southern gansu and northern shaanxi to sichuan); winters to myanmar
description: Medium-sized finch of hilly and montane forests and dense brushy forest edge. Male is the color of red wine, with crisp lilac eyebrows.

name: Speckle-chested Piculet
rangeDescription: Andes of northeastern peru in southeastern amazonas and northwestern san martín
description: Tiny woodpecker restricted to a small area of the Andes in northern Peru. Combination of dark breast marked with white spots and heavily barred belly separate it from other piculets in the region.

name: Orange Oriole
rangeDescription: Southeastern mexico (arid yucatán peninsula)
description: Attractive orange-and-black oriole of the Yucatan Peninsula, found in brushy woodland, forest edge, and semi-open areas with hedges and scattered trees. Rather similar to local population of Hooded Oriole, which often occurs in the same areas, even in the same flocks at flowering trees.
